claims.text: A roughly 5 nm AlN capping layer can provide high thermal conductivity at the nanoribbon interface.
Adding the AlN cap will improve heat extraction from as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi nanoribbons.
Improved interface heat extraction will reduce local thermal gradients during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Reducing local thermal gradients will permit a higher magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
Reducing local thermal gradients will reduce thermal hysteresis.
The AlN cap will not significantly perturb the intrinsic magnetocaloric transition.
The magnetocaloric transition or peak temperature of the capped nanoribbons will remain close to the bulk transition temperature.
Low-temperature ALD can produce uniform, conformal AlN coverage while preserving the original nanoribbon structure.
Additional deposition-related thermal budget could alter thin-film morphology.
The AlN cap will slightly alter surface stress distributions.
The AlN cap will preserve the inner microstructure of the alloy.
Accelerated heat removal will produce a faster temperature drop during magnetic-cooling cycles.
Accelerated heat removal will make the magnetocaloric phase transition more reversible.
Capped nanoribbons will have less thermal lag than the as-deposited baseline.
Capped nanoribbons will exhibit narrower magnetic hysteresis loops than the as-deposited baseline.
Uncapped as-deposited nanoribbons have slower heat extraction, lower cycle frequencies, and higher hysteresis because of persistent localized thermal gradients.
An ultrathin cap may modify surface magnetic properties or induce stress changes that affect the magnetocaloric peak.
